emerging_technology: Ex vivo CRISPR-edited autologous cell therapy
intended_application: Assess whether to build a referral and care-coordination pathway for eligible sickle-cell patients receiving an approved edited-cell therapy at a specialist center.
business_need: Improve access to specialist evaluation while maintaining informed choice and long-term follow-up.
users_stakeholders: Patients, hematologists, caregivers, specialist centers, payers
capabilities_constraints: Assume hematology staff and referral systems exist; no transplant unit, reimbursement agreement or qualified treatment center on site.
risk_consequence_context: Conditioning, treatment and follow-up carry serious clinical and financial consequences; eligibility and consent are individualized.
management_question: Should the network fund a referral pathway in 2027, and what evidence and partnerships must precede a decision?
additional_context: Hypothetical teaching case created 2026-11-16 for a prospective 2027 decision; organizational details and the proposed monitoring trigger are assumptions, not observations or forecasts. Conventional baseline: Existing individualized sickle-cell care and eligible established therapies. Complement or dependency: Specialist treatment centers, coordinated follow-up and coverage. Proposed monitoring trigger and owner: Clinical lead reviews quarterly; revisit on verified label, long-term safety, payer coverage or qualified-center capacity changes; patient decisions remain with clinicians. Hype-sensitive assertion to test, not a fact: CRISPR makes treatment low-risk, universally accessible, or appropriate for every patient.
